_comment: Physics profile for the UR5e under Isaac Sim, consumed by run_isaac_sim.py.
Joint names and home pose must match the IsaacSystem block in
cho_description_ur/urdf/ur5e.urdf. The UR arm is position-controlled only,
so there is no hand and no torque/velocity gain set in use.
_home_comment: Matches the <state_interface> initial_value entries in ur5e.urdf.
_armature_comment: Rotor inertia from the MuJoCo model (xml/ur5e.xml: <joint armature='0.1'> for every joint). NVIDIA's ur5e.usd authors none, but armature was decisive for the Franka wrist and costs nothing here.
_position_gain_comment: MuJoCo's actuator gains for this arm (xml/ur5e.xml): class size3 (shoulder_pan,
shoulder_lift, elbow) uses gainprm 20000 / biasprm -2500, class size1 (the three
wrists) uses 10000 / -1500. Those are already per-radian and consistently damped.
NVIDIA's ur5e.usd instead authors per-joint stiffness 9400/10021/10230/3941/3941/1000
in per-DEGREE units (538k-57k per radian) with damping 0.004-4, which is far stiffer
and essentially undamped - it works there only because the drive saturates at
maxForce 150/28 and behaves bang-bang. The MuJoCo numbers are the project's own
reference for this robot, so they are what is used.
_friction_comment: NVIDIA's ur5e.usd authors no joint friction. Unlike the Franka torque bringup, the UR runs position-controlled drives that dissipate on their own, so there is nothing here that needs the plant to settle it.
